title: Copilot Studio: interactive MCP apps render inside agent conversations
summary: The briefing matches the roadmap and the Microsoft documentation read for this check. The updated billing page still supports the quoted standard-harness rate and the distinction from Microsoft Copilot harness billing; the page appropriately leaves app-specific rendering prices and enforcement questions open.

claims.claim: Agent 365 and Copilot Studio can have separate controls, so a block is not documented as universal across products.

claims.claim: The standard-harness MCP overview says changes to server tools and resources are reflected dynamically.
claims.quote: When you update or remove tools and resources on the MCP server, Copilot Studio dynamically reflects these changes.

claims.claim: The prerelease Microsoft Copilot harness how-to tells makers to edit the server entry to refresh its connection and re-read changed tools.
claims.quote: If a server's URL, authentication, or exposed tools change after you add it, edit the server entry in the same **Tools** dialog to refresh the connection and re-read the tool list.

claims.claim: After Block in a new data policy, the documented procedure continues through Next, scope when prompted, Next, review and Create policy.
claims.quote: Review your policy, and then select **Create policy** if you're creating a new policy or **Update policy** if you're editing an existing policy.

claims.claim: The data policy page does not mention MCP apps specifically, although it explicitly includes agents and connector-backed MCP tools.
claims.quote: Searched: MCP apps in the fetched Configure data policies for agents text. Read its scope, MCP connector blocking and configuration sections; it names connected MCP servers, not MCP apps. The briefing separately states the documented general reach.

claims.claim: The read sources do not state that existing agents automatically change to render MCP apps.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio MCP apps tenant disable rendering resourceUri default switch. Read roadmap, MCP apps and server setup; they describe UI-enabled tool invocation, not a mandatory migration or automatic conversion of existing agents.
